items.title: Open-Weight Models Aren't Enough: Stanford HAI's James Landay Calls for Truly Open-Source AI
items.summary_en: In an opinion piece amid the U.S. policy debate over Chinese open-weight models (e.g., DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen, Moonshot's Kimi) narrowing the capability gap with U.S. labs, Stanford HAI Denning Director James Landay argues the debate is framed the wrong way. He distinguishes 'open-weight' models (only released weights) from truly 'open-source' models aligned with the Linux Foundation's Model Openness Framework, which also release code, training data, and tooling for outside scrutiny. Landay argues universities, not companies, are best positioned to build genuinely open frontier AI systems for science and society.
